item.content:encoded:
Tracfone joins the Be My Eyes Service Directory, allowing customers to connect directly with trained specialists via live video for real-time visual assistance.

SAN FRANCISCO — 26th of August, 2026 — Be My Eyes, the world’s leading accessibility platform for people who are blind or have low vision, today announced a new partnership with Tracfone, one of America’s leading wireless service providers. Tracfone has officially joined the Be My Eyes Service Directory, enabling blind and low vision customers across the U.S. to connect with trained Tracfone specialists via live video call for 24/7 dedicated support.

Through the free Be My Eyes app, Tracfone customers can now get real-time visual assistance simply by pointing their smartphone camera at their phone packaging, screen, or device. Tracfone specialists can see what the customer sees and provide step-by-step guidance on everyday wireless tasks, including activating a new device or SIM card, refilling service plans, setting up digital features, or troubleshooting network connectivity issues.

How It Works

  1. Open the App: Customers open the free Be My Eyes app on iOS or Android.
  2. Find Tracfone: In the screen-reader-friendly Service Directory, customers navigate to the Devices & Digital Services category and select Tracfone.
  3. Connect 24/7: A simple tap initiates a secure, live video call connecting the user directly to a trained Tracfone customer support specialist within seconds.
  4. Get Real-Time Assistance: Using the smartphone camera, the Tracfone representative provides clear, hands-free verbal guidance to resolve technical or physical setup tasks independently.

“Reliable mobile service is a necessity for navigating modern life, but setting up a device, swapping a SIM card, or checking serial numbers on packaging can create unnecessary visual barriers,” said Mike Buckley, CEO of Be My Eyes. “By bringing trained specialists into our Service Directory 24/7, Tracfone is demonstrating a real commitment to accessibility. Together, we’re ensuring their blind and low vision customers have the fast, secure, and independent support they deserve, whenever they need it.”

The addition of Tracfone expands the growing roster of global telecommunications and consumer service leaders leveraging Be My Eyes Service Connect to deliver fully inclusive, accessible customer care.

To learn more about Be My Eyes or to explore how your company can join the Service Directory, visit bemyeyes.com.

About Be My Eyes

Be My Eyes is a global network that connects blind and low-vision individuals with sighted volunteers and company representatives for visual assistance through live video calls and AI technology. Serving more than 1 million blind and low-vision users through a network of 10 million volunteers across 150+ countries and 180+ languages, Be My Eyes is on a mission to make the world more accessible to everyone.

About Tracfone

Tracfone Wireless provides quality no-contract wireless solutions to value-conscious consumers and is available at more than 90,000 retail locations nationwide, as well as at tracfone.com. 

Tracfone is part of the Verizon Value portfolio of prepaid brands, which includes Straight Talk, Total by Verizon, Visible, Simple Mobile, SafeLink, Walmart Family Mobile, and Verizon Prepaid. Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE, Nasdaq: VZ) is one of the world’s leading providers of technology, communications, information and entertainment products and services. 

For more information on Tracfone, visit tracfone.com.

The post Be My Eyes Partners with Tracfone to Bring 24/7 Accessible Customer Support to Blind and Low Vision Users appeared first on Be My Eyes.

item.content:encoded:
At its heart, cooking centers on gathering the people we love, sharing stories across the table, and creating those warm family moments that linger long after the last bite. Through our partnership with Barilla, we are on a mission to make culinary experiences fully accessible, helping blind and low-vision home chefs prepare their favorite meals safely and with total confidence.

Real Stories: Daniel’s Kitchen Adventures

To truly understand the impact of visual assistance in the kitchen, look no further than Daniel Martinez from Brownsville, Texas. Daniel works as a Pre-Employment Transition Specialist Trainer, dedicated advocate, and mentor for youth and adults who are blind. As a tech enthusiast, Be My Eyes is a core tool in his daily independent living toolkit.

For Daniel, cooking a pasta dish with stoves and other cooking appliances presents unique visual challenges. But paired with his hands-free smart glasses, Be My Eyes connected him to a dedicated Barilla agent who provided real-time, critical feedback to help him cook the perfect Alfredo pasta.

During one dinner prep, Be My Eyes proved essential when Daniel accidentally dropped uncooked pasta onto a lit burner. To avoid burning himself on the hot stove, he relied on instant visual guidance to clear the hazard away from the flame safely. He also used the app to verify settings on his non-accessible cooking appliance, effortlessly confirming the correct cooking time and temperature.

For Daniel, the true value of Be My Eyes lies in immediate autonomy. While it’s often easy to wait for a sighted family member or roommate to return home to answer a visual question, having instantaneous access through your smartphone or smart glasses fosters immediate independence and keeps everyday momentum going.

How to Reach Out to Barilla on Be My Eyes

We are continuously collaborating with Barilla to expand accessible cooking initiatives, recipe guides, and inclusive product features. Whether you have feedback on Barilla’s packaging, ideas for accessible recipes, or inquiries regarding our ongoing accessibility partnership, getting in touch is simple.

Barilla is available in the Be My Eyes Service Directory, meaning you can connect directly with a Barilla representative for accessible support. Open the Be My Eyes app and find Barilla in the Service Directory to get inspired. Or visit their profile at this link.

If you don’t have Be My Eyes yet, you can download our app for your smartphone or tablet and join our growing community today: download now on iOS or Android.

The post NatWest Partners with Be My Eyes to Launch Pilot Project Aiming to Make Banking More Accessible for Blind and Low Vision customers  appeared first on Be My Eyes.
item.content:encoded:
• NatWest is the first UK bank to partner with Be My Eyes using Service Directory and Service Connect, the world’s largest support platform for blind and low vision people.
  • The upcoming pilot will see a selected group of blind and low vision customers access real-time, secure visual support from trained NatWest colleagues via video calls.
  • Led by NatWest’s Open Innovation team, the free pilot supports the Bank’s ambition to provide an accessible experience for all customers.

Friday 21st August 2026 – NatWest has announced it will work with global accessibility platform Be My Eyes to use live visual assistance to help blind or low vision customers manage everyday banking tasks more easily and independently.

Through a pilot with the Be My Eyes app, a selected group of customers will be able to make secure video calls supported by NatWest.

The pilot will see a select group of customers take part in the app by accessing a Service Directory and selecting NatWest. Within seconds and via a single tap, users will be placed on a video call with a trained NatWest colleague.

At this point, the customer’s phone camera or smart glasses become the colleague’s eyes, allowing them to guide the customer through the relevant journey in real time.

This enables colleagues to provide clear, verbal guidance to help customers complete tasks with greater confidence and independence. The pilot could assist a number of day-to-day banking activities including reading a letter or activating a new card. 

The service is free and simple to use, with no appointments required. 

As part of the pilot, NatWest’s Open Innovation team will work in partnership with Be My Eyes to identify further opportunities where live visual support could improve the banking experience for blind or low vision customers. 

Insights from the pilot will help inform the next phase of the programme, including opportunities to make the pilot available to more customers later in 2026.

Register your interest in the Pilot
If you are a NatWest customer and would like to register your interest in participating in the pilot, you can learn more by emailing andy.lane@bemyeyes.com.

ENDS 

Notes to editors

Innovation at NatWest Group

The Open Innovation team at NatWest Group have a vision to lead the future of banking by aligning the external technology ecosystem with the bank’s strategy, to inspire new products and services for our customers, colleagues and communities.

NatWest Group has stringent security measures in place to protect its customers. Customers will never be asked to share PINs, passwords or security details as part of this support.

About Be My Eyes

Be My Eyes started with a simple idea: to make the world more accessible for blind and low-vision people through the power of connection.

The idea came from Hans Jørgen Wiberg, a low vision Danish craftsman. While working with The Danish Association of the Blind, Hans noticed how often people needed a little visual assistance for everyday tasks. A friend shared how video calls with family helped him get that assistance, and Hans saw an opportunity: what if blind and low-vision people could connect with a global network of volunteers, ready to lend their sight?  
   
In 2015, the Be My Eyes app was launched and, within 24 hours, 10,000 volunteers had signed up. Today, millions of volunteers support users in over 180 languages – proving that a little help goes a long way.   

Enterprise partners include Microsoft, Google, Procter & Gamble, Hilton, and Tesco. Be My Eyes was named among Time’s Best Inventions of 2023 and has won an Apple Design Award.

For more information, visit bemyeyes.com

item.dc:creator: michele

item.content:encoded:
Two recent testimonials show how AI-powered accessibility is helping blind employees at Envision Xpress work more independently, collaborate more effectively, and navigate today’s digital workplace with greater confidence.

If your business would like to support blind employees better at work, then explore Workplace and request a demo here.

The modern workplace is filled with visual information. PDFs, screenshots, spreadsheets, customer-submitted photos, dashboards, and web platforms are essential to getting work done, but they often present significant accessibility barriers for blind and low vision employees.

That’s exactly why we built Be My Eyes Workplace: to complement existing assistive technology and provide AI-powered visual assistance designed specifically for professional environments.

Recently, we received two thoughtful testimonials from blind professionals at Envision Xpress, testing Be My Eyes Workplace in customer service and eCommerce roles. Their experiences highlight how the product is helping bridge accessibility gaps that traditional screen readers alone cannot always address.

Making inaccessible documents accessible

One of the most frequently mentioned benefits was the ability to work independently with PDF documents.

Many workplace documents (purchase orders, receipts, invoices, shipping records, and scanned forms) are difficult or impossible to navigate with a screen reader alone. Be My Eyes Workplace allows employees to upload these documents, ask follow-up questions, and have an ongoing conversation with AI about their contents.

One tester shared that this conversational approach has transformed how they review complex documents and internal systems. Rather than simply extracting text, Workplace helps locate specific customer numbers, item numbers, and other critical information, even providing guidance for navigating complex interfaces.

“The system is able to identify customer numbers, item numbers, and other important data. It can also guide me by explaining how many lines I need to move up or down within the function to find the exact information I am looking for.”

Beyond text: Understanding visual information

Today’s work isn’t just about documents. Employees regularly receive screenshots, product photos, proof-of-delivery forms, and visually rich interfaces that can be difficult to interpret using a screen reader alone.

One tester explained that Be My Eyes Workplace has become especially valuable when reviewing customer-submitted photos of damaged products. Instead of relying on a colleague to describe an image, they can independently evaluate visible damage and process replacement or refund requests more efficiently.

The same independence extends to email attachments and screenshots containing tracking information, order details, account information, or error messages.

“Screenshots often contain tracking information, order details, error messages, or account information that is inaccessible through a screen reader alone. Be My Eyes Workplace allows me to quickly understand the content of those screenshots and respond more independently.”

Working alongside screen readers

An important theme appeared in both testimonials: Be My Eyes Workplace isn’t intended to replace screen readers like JAWS, it enhances them.

Workplace fills many of the gaps where conventional accessibility tools struggle, including interpreting visually complex spreadsheets, describing table layouts, navigating platforms like Amazon Seller Central, and explaining unlabeled interface elements.

As one tester summarized:

“Be My Eyes Workplace does not replace my existing assistive technology, but instead works alongside JAWS to improve accessibility in areas where screen readers traditionally struggle.”

Creating a more collaborative workplace

In addition to AI-powered assistance, Be My Eyes Workplace includes the ability to securely connect with sighted colleagues for live visual assistance when needed. One tester noted the potential of this feature to strengthen collaboration across teams and suggested expanding access so more sighted employees can provide support whenever appropriate.

Independence that benefits everyone

Perhaps the most powerful message shared by both testers wasn’t about any single feature, it was about the confidence that comes from working more independently.

One employee concluded:

“Be My Eyes Workplace has significantly improved my ability to perform job tasks independently and efficiently as a blind employee.”

Another summarized the impact this way:

“The software has improved my efficiency, independence, and ability to complete tasks without needing as much assistance from coworkers.”

They also believe the benefits extend well beyond their own role.

“Based on my testing experience, I believe Be My Eyes Workplace would be a valuable accessibility tool for blind and visually impaired employees working in customer service and eCommerce environments.”

Similarly, the first tester concluded:

“Overall, Be My Eyes Workplace has provided meaningful accessibility improvements that support independence, workplace efficiency, and stronger collaboration between blind and sighted employees.”

As more organizations look for practical ways to improve workplace accessibility, testimonials like these demonstrate how AI can complement existing assistive technology, not replacing it, but helping blind professionals work more independently, efficiently, and confidently every day.

If your business would like to support blind employees better at work, then explore Workplace and request a demo here.

item.content:encoded:
Be My Eyes Workplace is now available for macOS alongside the launch of Be My Eyes for Mac, completing the Be My Eyes for Desktop experience across Windows and Mac.

Austin, TX, USA, July 6, 2026 — Be My Eyes today announced, at the National Federation for the Blind Annual Convention in Austin, Texas, the expansion of its desktop offerings to macOS, making both Be My Eyes Workplace and Be My Eyes for MacOS available to users worldwide. Together with the existing Windows applications, these releases complete the desktop family of products, delivering AI-powered visual assistance across the two most widely used desktop operating systems.

The launch represents a significant milestone in Be My Eyes’ mission to make digital experiences more accessible and inclusive. Whether at work or at home, blind and low vision users can now access the same powerful visual assistance experience on the desktop platform of their choice.

For individuals, Be My Eyes for Mac extends the company’s existing free Be My Eyes for Windows offering to macOS, providing access to Be My Eyes’ AI-powered visual assistance for personal everyday computing. Users can ask questions about what’s on their screen, receive contextual descriptions, and get help describing all manner of digital content—all from their Mac desktop. Collectively the Windows and MacOS offerings for personal use is known as Be My Eyes for Desktop.

For organizations and business use, Be My Eyes Workplace is also now available on macOS, enabling enterprises and other organizations to support their employees who are blind or have low vision with secure, AI-powered and trusted colleague workplace assistance. Designed specifically for professional environments, Be My Eyes Workplace helps employees independently interact with workplace applications, documents, dashboards, and digital workflows while providing enterprise-grade security, privacy controls, and centralized deployment, which are all critical for enterprise deployments.

“Desktop computing remains at the center of how people work, create, and communicate,” said Mike Buckley, CEO of Be My Eyes. “By bringing both our free consumer experience and our enterprise solution to macOS, we’re ensuring that blind and low vision users don’t have to choose between their preferred platform and accessible, AI-powered visual assistance. Be My Eyes is now available to our users no matter what computing platform they have.”

The expansion to macOS also provides organizations with greater flexibility when deploying accessible technology across mixed-device environments. Employees using either Windows or Mac can now benefit from a consistent Be My Eyes Workplace experience, simplifying IT deployment while helping create more inclusive workplaces.

The launch builds on Be My Eyes’ growing portfolio of AI-powered and hybrid accessibility solutions, combining advanced computer vision with conversational AI and person-to-person support that can help users understand visual information in real time. From interpreting charts and documents to navigating complex software interfaces, Be My Eyes Workplace brings visual assistance directly into the desktop workflow.

With today’s announcement, the Be My Eyes desktop portfolio includes:

  • Be My Eyes for Desktop — Free AI-powered visual assistance for personal use
    – Be My Eyes for Windows 
    – Be My Eyes for MacOS 
  • Be My Eyes Workplace (available on Windows and MacOS) — Enterprise-ready visual assistance designed for organizations and employees.

Be My Eyes for Mac is available free of charge for personal use only beginning today. Be My Eyes Workplace for Mac is available immediately for enterprise customers and organizations worldwide, and can be downloaded here.

About Be My Eyes

Be My Eyes connects blind and low vision people with AI-powered visual assistance and human support, making everyday tasks and digital experiences more accessible. Through its consumer and enterprise products, Be My Eyes empowers greater independence while helping organizations build more inclusive experiences for employees and customers around the world.

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco, CA – 15 June 2026 – Be My Eyes today announced the availability of its award-winning app on Huawei’s HarmonyOS operating system, bringing its volunteer-powered visual assistance service to people living in China who are blind or have low vision.

The initial release of the app brings the call-a-volunteer functionality to HarmonyOS, enabling blind and low vision users to connect with sighted volunteers through live video calls. The volunteers then provide real-time assistance with everyday tasks such as identifying products, reading labels, sorting items, and more.

The launch marks another important step in Be My Eyes’ underlying mission which is to make the world more accessible for people who are blind or have low vision , wherever they are, and whatever device or operating system they happen to use. With an estimated 17 million or more blind and low vision consumers living in China, this partnership brings Be My Eyes to a huge population of people who would otherwise have no access to it.

“Accessibility should not depend on which phone someone owns,” said Mike Buckley, CEO of Be My Eyes. “Our mission has always been to connect people who are blind or have low vision with assistance whenever and wherever they need it. By bringing Be My Eyes to HarmonyOS, we’re extending that mission to a new community of users and helping ensure that more people can access support on their terms.”

Since its founding, Be My Eyes has grown into one of the world’s largest communities focused on accessibility, connecting millions of volunteers with blind and low vision users across more than 200 countries and territories and in hundreds of languages. In China alone, Be My Eyes has 1.6 million sighted volunteers.

With a longer-term plan of bringing full app functionality, including AI assistance, to HarmonyOS, this first launch focuses initially with volunteer calling functionality – including private groups – allowing users to receive assistance from the community that has been at the heart of the service since its inception. Additional features and enhancements will be evaluated for future releases.

The launch reflects Be My Eyes’ long-standing commitment to platform accessibility and user choice. The organization has worked to make its services available across major mobile ecosystems so that blind and low vision users can access assistance on the devices that best meet their needs.

“Huawei users who are blind or have low vision deserve access to the same support and independence as anyone else,” Buckley added. “This launch is about reaching more people, removing barriers, and ensuring accessibility is available wherever it is needed.”

The Be My Eyes app for HarmonyOS is available beginning today through Huawei’s AppGallery and can be downloaded from Download Be My Eyes for HarmonyOS

About Be My Eyes

Launched in 2015, Be My Eyes is a globally recognized and award-winning Accessibility Management provider for people who are blind or have low vision. With a global community of over one million users, and more than 10 million volunteers, Be My Eyes connects blind and low vision users with sighted volunteers and companies, through live video and AI to tackle inaccessible parts of everyday life, whether at home or at work; all for free to the end user. Be My Eyes is available in more than 200 countries and territories worldwide and its volunteers speak more than 180 languages.To learn more, please visit bemyeyes.com and bemyeyes.com/business

item.content:encoded:
Stay up to date with the latest from Be My Eyes! From the workplace to the wider world, we’ve got a lot to share. This edition covers new tools for blind and low vision professionals, a closer look at the Groups feature, inspiring community stories, and the latest from our partner at Hilton. Plus, discover where you’ll find us this summer. Let’s dive in.

Discover Be My Eyes Workplace

For the working part of your life, we’d like to introduce you to Be My Eyes Workplace. Built for blind and low vision professionals, Workplace brings AI-powered visual assistance, real-time colleague support, and accessible file descriptions together in one place, everything you need to navigate your professional world independently.

Explore Workplace Here

Call people you know on Be My Eyes with Be My Eyes Groups

Did you know Be My Eyes has a group feature? Our volunteers are wonderful, but sometimes a familiar voice makes more sense, for questions that are a bit personal, or when someone already knows your home and your setup. With groups, you can call people you already know and trust, whether that’s family, friends, or colleagues, right alongside our 10 million+ volunteers.

Find out how to set up your first group

Here’s what blind and low vision guests are saying about Be My Eyes at Hilton

Since October 2024, Hilton has been part of the Be My Eyes Service Directory, meaning you can instantly connect through Be My Eyes with a trained Hilton team member who can see through your phone’s camera and help you navigate your room, on your schedule. We asked guests what they thought.

Read the full story here

Why accessible technology matters most where it’s least available

340 million people are blind or have low vision. 90% of them live in emerging economies, where most accessibility tools are either unavailable or unaffordable. Be My Eyes is free, low-bandwidth, and powered by a global volunteer network. For communities where disability support is underfunded and specialist services are scarce, that makes it something more than an app.

Read more

Meet us at Vis-Ability and VivaTech this summer

We’re heading out to meet the world this summer. You’ll find us at Vis-Ability 2026 in London on June 10, joining senior leaders to explore the future of accessibility and employment in the UK. Then in July, we’ll be at VivaTech in Paris, one of Europe’s biggest innovation events, looking at what emerging technology means for inclusion. If you’re attending either event, we’d love to connect.

Discover where to find us

How Be My Eyes Became Part of Sana’s Everyday Life

Sana has been totally blind since birth. She’s also Global Chief Privacy Officer at a multinational engineering firm. And she hasn’t gone a day without Be My Eyes since a friend used the app to check her lipstick.

Discover Sana’s Story

One Engineer’s Blueprint for Life After Vision Loss

When Syed lost his vision in 2005 after being shot during a robbery, he rebuilt his life from scratch. Today he holds a master’s in computer science and works as an accessibility engineer at the American Foundation for the Blind.

Discover Syed’s Story

Subscribe to the Newsletter

Are you a blind or low-vision Be My Eyes user who wants to receive these updates directly in your inbox? Follow these steps to subscribe:

  1. Navigate to the Settings tab in the Be My Eyes app.
  2. Click on Notifications.
  3. Activate the slider to accept marketing communications.

The post Did You Know? Be My Eyes Groups appeared first on Be My Eyes.
item.content:encoded:
While our volunteers are wonderful, there are times when calling a stranger can feel overwhelming or like you’re being too familiar with someone you don’t know. There are questions better answered by people you already trust.

There’s an answer to that. In case you’ve missed it, Be My Eyes has a group feature.

Along with calling one of our over 10 million volunteers, you also have the option of calling people you know. You can have other blind and low vision people in the same group with you, in case there are several who are in your same social circles.

What to know

  • There can be up to 20 people per group
  • A group can have a mix of blind, low vision, and sighted members
  • When a blind or low vision person calls a group, the call only goes to sighted volunteers
  • You can create up to five groups

That structure lets you split things naturally. Family, friends, work, or whatever makes sense for you.

How to create a group

  1. Go to the Get Support tab
  2. Select Groups
  3. Select Manage Groups
  4. Choose Create Group
  5. Add people and send them an invite link

How to make a call

You can call your group in a similar way to how you would call a volunteer. In the Get Support tab, hit “Groups,” then the group you’d like to call.

If you are using smart glasses like Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses or Oakley Meta smart glasses, you can do it hands-free. For example, if your group is called “Family,” just say:

“Hey Meta, call Family with Be My Eyes.”

When to use a group instead of a volunteer

Use a group when context matters. If someone already knows your home, your setup, or what you are trying to do, you will spend less time explaining and more time getting an answer. It can also feel more comfortable for questions that are a bit more personal or specific.

Volunteers are still there. This just gives you another option when a familiar voice makes more sense.

The post Did You Know? Be My Eyes Groups appeared first on Be My Eyes.

item.dc:creator: Mike Buckley
item.description:

The post Respect, Trust, and Scale: A Note to Our Community appeared first on Be My Eyes.
item.content:encoded:
A few weeks ago Be My Eyes reached a major milestone — one million blind and low vision users and over 10 million volunteers.

A volunteer helps someone check an expiry date. 

A caller gets quick support navigating a screen. 

A small, human connection makes a big difference.

These moments are powerful precisely because they are respectful and built on trust.

Recently, we’ve seen concerns about volunteers sharing videos of their calls or experiences on social media. While this is a rare occurrence — fewer than 0.002% of our call volumes (meaning that out of 1.5 million calls, there would be 30 instances of this) – assisting a blind person should never be performative entertainment or “good social content.” One of our blind employees compared this to “The Truman Show” — a movie about a man who discovers his entire life has been televised without his consent, with everyone around him in on it. It feels horrible. Posting a “look how cool it was to help a blind person” video is dehumanizing, and we need to acknowledge and address that.

So first, let’s be clear: this behavior is not acceptable and is a violation of our Terms of Service.

Second, the Be My Eyes platform provides a number of security features about which some of our users may not be aware. Be My Eyes Groups for example allows users to define their own trusted groups of individuals – perhaps their friends or family members – for sensitive or private call topics. But the hard part of some of these volunteer video posts is that almost all feature recording via a separate device, completely outside of our app experience. So a volunteer may have a friend or a separate camera recording the interaction. This makes technological “in-app policing” of this ineffective.

Third, we have and will continue to issue takedown requests when we discover posts like these. Social media companies are often slow to act and sometimes don’t respond at all, but we occasionally have success. We remove and ban volunteers when we can connect a post to a specific account. We also continue to educate volunteers, and wrote about this issue in our most recent volunteer newsletter — something we will repeat.

But clearly, there is more we can do. We continue, and indeed are increasing, our social media monitoring on this issue. We are also constantly evaluating additional technological and human solutions and will report back.

In the interim, let’s work together to attack this. When we become aware of a post like this, we will act. You can also help us if you want. If you become aware of a post like this that violates our terms,  please notify us at community@bemyeyes.com. When we receive these reports, we will investigate and a) issue takedown requests; b) attempt to identify the volunteer in our system and warn and/or ban them; and c) when possible, comment on the post directly, noting that it violates our terms of service.

But let’s be honest with each other. We are not going to be perfect here. We are a rapidly growing community of more than 11 million people, and any group of that size will have issues and individuals who make poor choices. But by working together, we can mitigate and minimize those issues.

To our blind and low-vision community: we continue to listen and learn. We appreciate you holding us accountable. And we’re committed to continuous improvement.

To our volunteers: Your generosity is what makes this platform extraordinary. Respecting boundaries is part of that generosity.

And to everyone watching this space: When you operate at a global scale like we do, even rare issues can become visible and important. What matters is the response — and we’re committed to responding with clarity and accountability, and a passion for doing better every day.

item.content:encoded:
Travel is better when you’re in control. You know which channel has the morning news. You can figure out the thermostat without relying on anyone. You move through a hotel stay on your own terms. That’s the experience every guest deserves.

Since October 2024, Hilton has been part of Be My Eyes Service Directory. Open the app, tap Hilton in the directory, and you’re instantly connected to a trained Hilton team member who can see through your phone camera and assist you with whatever you need in your room. All on your schedule, without waiting in a front-desk queue.

What Guests Are Already Doing With It

Be My Eyes users have been putting the service to good use since day one. Here’s a taste of what people are actually using it for:

“I used to have to rely only on the front desk, but sometimes they’re very busy helping other guests. This adds a second layer of help. It feels like having a virtual personal assistant at my fingertips.” — Jose, Be My Eyes Users

“Knowing that Hilton partners with Be My Eyes tells me accessibility is being taken seriously, not as an afterthought, but as part of how they do business.” — Jeremy, Be My Eyes users.

Even the person who started it all has become a regular user. Hans Jørgen Wiberg — the founder of Be My Eyes himself, who also has low-vision — tried the Hilton service in a recent stay during CSUN 2026. 

Here’s what he had to say:

“I woke up early, maybe jetlag, or just being 62, I don’t know. I wanted the news. Called Hilton on Be My Eyes, took a few minutes to sort out the TV, and now I’m watching ABC News. This is pretty good!”— Hans Jørgen Wiberg, Founder of Be My Eyes

Watch Matthew & Paul Try It Out

Our friends Matthew, Paul and Mr Maple took Be My Eyes for a spin during their Hilton stay — check out what happened!

What Can You Actually Use It For?

Here are some of the most common (and most useful) ways guests are using Be My Eyes during their Hilton experience:

  • Navigating your room on arrival — Get oriented quickly. Ask a Hilton agent to walk you through the layout, locate the switches, safe, or USB ports, and get comfortable faster.
  • Operating the TV — Find your inputs, switch sources, or hunt down the right channel without fumbling through an unfamiliar remote.
  • Reading in-room materials — Menus, compendiums, amenity labels, laundry instructions — anything printed in your room can be read aloud to you in seconds.
  • Adjusting climate controls — Thermostats vary wildly across hotel rooms. Get it set to exactly what you want, first try.
  • Checking accessibility features — Confirm grab bar locations, lighting setups, or furniture arrangements before you need them.
  • Ordering food or services — Navigate the in-room dining menu or figure out how to reach specific hotel services without guessing.

How to Get Started

  1. Download the Be My Eyes app (free on iOS and Android)
  2. Go to Service Directory and navigate to Hotels & Accommodation
  3. Search for Hilton
  4. Start a Call: a trained Hilton team member picks up

That’s it. Available across Hilton properties in the US and Canada!
